title: Oregon State Police: In-Custody Death Investigation - child killer Richard Wayne Godwin (DOB: ~1945 / Age: 77)

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Oregon State Police: In-Custody Death Investigation - child killer Richard Wayne Godwin (DOB: ~1945 / Age: 77)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law (ORS 192.314 to 192.478), I hereby request copies of all public records, documents, and visual media held, created, or received by the Oregon State Police regarding OSP's involvement in, or assistance with, the in-custody death of Richard Wayne Godwin, who died on or about October 2, 2022, while incarcerated at the Snake River Correctional Institution (SRCI).

I am aware, based on the Oregon Department of Corrections' public news release on this death, that Mr. Godwin passed away in the SRCI infirmary while on hospice care, and that OSP was notified "as with all in-custody deaths" as a matter of standard agency protocol. I recognize this may mean OSP's role was limited to notification and liaison rather than a full criminal investigation. Accordingly, this request is intended to capture whatever record exists documenting OSP's role — whether that is a complete investigative case file or a brief notification/liaison record — and is not limited to records that would only exist if a criminal investigation had been opened.

For guidance, here is a link to an Oregon Department of Corrections press release regarding the in-custody death of Richard Wayne Godwin: 
https://flashalert.net/id/ORCorrections/157984#:~:text=An%20Oregon%20Department%20of%20Corrections%20(DOC)%20adult,11,%202026.%20Godwin%20was%2077%20years%20old

I. SPECIFICALLY REQUESTED RECORDS

Please conduct a search of OSP Major Crimes, Criminal Investigations Division, Detective Division, and Region/Post records for Malheur County / SRCI. This request includes, but is not limited to, the following categories of records, to the extent they exist:

Case Identification: Any OSP case, incident, or report number assigned in connection with this death, and the classification under which the matter was logged (e.g., "Death Investigation," "Non-Criminal Death," "Assist Other Agency," or equivalent).

Investigative Reports & Case Files: All OSP Detective Case Files, initial responder notes, supplementary incident reports, investigative summaries, lead sheets, crime/incident scene processing reports, and administrative logs regarding OSP's involvement or assistance — or, if no formal case file was opened, whatever notification, liaison, or closure memo documents OSP's role and its determination that no further investigation was warranted.

Evidence & Property Logs: Complete evidence ledgers, property receipts, chain-of-custody forms, and lists of physical or digital evidence gathered by OSP personnel, if any were generated.

Interview Audio, Video, & Transcripts: Audio recordings, video recordings, notes, or verbatim transcripts of any witness interviews, inmate/cellmate statements, or staff or medical personnel interviews conducted by OSP officers.

Scene Documentation & Media: a. High-resolution copies of all crime/death scene digital photographs taken by OSP investigators. b. Any surveillance camera or CCTV footage collected by OSP from SRCI or ODOC as evidence.

Communications & Dispatch Records: CAD (Computer Aided Dispatch) event logs, 911/dispatch audio recordings, agency-to-agency notifications (between OSP, ODOC, Malheur County Sheriff's Office, and Malheur County District Attorney), and internal OSP emails or teletypes discussing this matter.

Medical Examiner / Autopsy Correspondence: Copies of any records in OSP's possession from the Oregon State Medical Examiner or Malheur County Medical Examiner concerning the cause and manner of death.

II. STATUTORY TIMELINES & PROCEDURES

Pursuant to ORS 192.329:

Please acknowledge receipt of this request within five (5) business days.

Please complete the processing of this request as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay (statutorily defined as no later than 15 business days following receipt, unless an extension applies under ORS 192.329(5)).

III. SEGREGABILITY AND REDACTION NOTICE

If OSP determines that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure under Oregon law, please note that ORS 192.338 requires the public body to release all non-exempt, reasonably segregable portions of the records.

If any document, photograph, or media file is withheld or redacted in full or in part:

Identify the specific statutory exemption claimed for each redaction or withholding — for example, ORS 192.355(2)(b) (images of a dead body) or ORS 192.345(36) (medical examiner reports), as applicable — rather than a general citation to Oregon public records law.

Provide a brief description of the material withheld.

State the basis for applying the exemption to a death that occurred in October 2022, where no criminal proceedings resulted and the subject is deceased. For any withholding under ORS 192.355(2)(b) specifically, please address whether the public interest in disclosure — including public oversight of ODOC's hospice and infirmary care and OSP's protocols for reviewing custodial deaths — outweighs the privacy interest the exemption is meant to protect.

IV. FEE WAIVER / PUBLIC INTEREST REQUEST

Pursuant to ORS 192.324(5), I request a reduction or complete waiver of any processing fees. Release of these records primarily benefits the general public by fostering transparency, oversight, and public confidence in the administration of justice, state law enforcement operations, and the conditions and quality of medical/hospice care within Oregon Department of Corrections facilities. This request is made for public oversight and historical/educational research, not for commercial use.

If a fee waiver is denied and the estimated fees to fulfill this request exceed $25.00, please provide an itemized estimate of the costs prior to commencing work, as required by ORS 192.324(4)(c).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: AI Policies and Emails
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any policies relating to the usage of Large language models, and other "AI".

Retention policies of AI/LLM chat logs and image creations.

From January 1 2022 to the present: 

1) A log of emails sent and/or received between current or former Seattle Public Schools employees and any contracted workers and the following domains:

@openai.com
@chatgpt.com
@anthropic.com
@claude.ai
@gab.ai
@jasper.ai

2) A log of emails sent and/or received between current or former Seattle Public Schools employees and any contracted workers and the following addresses:
m365copilotupdates@microsoft.com
microsoft365copilot@communication.microsoft.com
google-gemini-noreply@google.com

To make things simpler, this request does not include the contents of the emails. The information I am hoping for is: Recipient, sender, date received/sent, and subject line.

I believe this should be exportable via Google Vault or Microsoft Purview.

If your agency has a retention policy for this data shorter than this I would be grateful if you informed me so I can adjust my request time frame.

I would prefer the data in text searchable formats, such as CSV or Excel, if possible.

If you have any questions or wish to clarify any part of this request feel free to let me know. If this request is too wide, feel free to contact me to explore the possibility of adjusting the scope of this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Olivia

title: Correspondence Between DOS and ALPR Vendors

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Correspondence Between DOS and ALPR Vendors
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am looking for a few pieces of information related to:
CR26-0246, a contract between the city of Denver and Axon Enterprise Inc. allowing for the purchase and install of multiple ALPR Units (https://denver.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=7938541&GUID=093F64CB-3951-4C69-9B4B-14B57D302CA6&Options=&Search=)
Denver Police Department had a pilot program and then a contract with Flock Safety that the police found very useful. They then cancelled that contract and entered into a new contract with Axon Enterprise Inc. I'm hoping to find out what about the old system or the old vendor police and/or city leadership didn't like, as well as what they do like about this new system. I’d also like to find out what the police hoped to get out of the old system, how they talked about it internally, and what they are hoping to get out of the new system.

Please provide the following: 

1. The planned locations, or current locations of the ALPR Units from contract POLIC-202683606

2. Contract POLIC-202683606

3. Correspondence (emails, memos, instant messages, etc.) sent internally or DPD/DOS employee to Vendors of ALPR’s.
To reduce the burden and scope of this request, please limit correspondence to items dated between Jan 1, 2022 to the time this request is processed.
To further reduce the burden and scope of the request, limit correspondence with ALPR vendors to employees or parties representing Flock Safety and Axon Enterprise, Inc. (for emails: addresses ending in @flocksafety.com; @axon.com)
To further reduce the burden and scope of the request, please return correspondence with subject line or contents including key phrases such as:
Flock
Flock Safety
25-0413
ALPR
LPR
LPR's
Axon ALPR
Axon LPR
CR26-0246
CR 26-0246
CR 26 0246
26-0246
POLIC-202683606
202683606
Surveillance
Surveillance Task Force

Finally, to further limit the burden and scope of this request, limit correspondence to items where the following parties are either a sender or recipient:
Ron Thomas, Chief of Police
Al Gardner, Deputy Mayor
Emily Lauck, Policy Director
Commander Cliff Barnes, Director of DPD Cyber Bureau
Jacob Hererra
Todd Ericson

For email and other applicable mediums of correspondence, please include attachments.

I appreciate the possibility that even after the attempted limiting of scope and burden, there may still be a considerable amount of items that fit this request. Please let me know if this is the case and I will do my best to further refine the scope of the search.

Thank you for your help,
William Beckett
Resident of the Baker Neighborhood, Denver

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

Good afternoon-

This email is being sent in response to your CORA request submitted on May 20, 2026. Please find the Department’s responses to each item of your request outlined below.

  1.
The planned locations, or current locations of the ALPR Units from contract POLIC-20268360

Please visit https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Police-Department/Safety-and-Crime-Prevention/Auto-Theft-Prevention and navigate to "Additional Resources” on the right-hand side, where you will find the ALPR locations map.

  1.
Contract POLIC-202683606

See attached.

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Westfield Police Department)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Westfield Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

Please provide responsive records in their original electronic format where reasonably available. For databases, audit logs, search logs, reports, or tabular records, I prefer CSV, XLS/XLSX, or another native machine-readable format rather than PDF printouts.

This request seeks existing government records and does not require the agency to create a new record. If a requested list or summary does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing report, export, audit log, configuration record, or other record containing the requested information.

In advance of filing this request, Flock Safety was consulted regarding the availability of these records. Flock Safety indicated that if an agency administrator has difficulty locating relevant audit or system records, the administrator may contact Flock Safety for support.

If any portion of a responsive record is considered exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt portion and provide the remainder of the record. Please identify the specific legal basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: IHSC SENs and SIRs
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

An IHSC record showing the number, by month and year if possible, of Significant Event Notifications (SENs), Significant Incident Reports (SIRs), or similar records IHSC received for the period beginning January 1, 2021, and continuing through May 5, 2025, in which ICE ERO Field Office staff, ICE detention contractors, or IHSC Field Medical Coordinators who submitted the SEN or SIR checked the box next to "Death in Custody or Operations", "Hospital Admission," "Emergency Department Visit (ED", or "Serious Health Incidents Affected Bedspace Volume".

Here is an example of SEN/SIR data from a single ICE detention facility provided in response to a prior FOIA: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/25469567-aurora-medical-sens-sirs-2023-icfo-03979-001/. I am seeking a report from the IHSC system of records the government's detention medical supervisors use to track and monitor these SENs and SIRs at facilities nationwide. I am willing to discuss narrowing or altering this requests should IHSC have a more efficient means of providing something similar to allow for data analysis. 

I seek expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and declare under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and understanding: 
1. I am a member of the media primarily engaged in information dissemination, and I have been granted expedited processing on this basis previously by federal FOIA agencies.  Examples of my edited works are available here: https://theappeal.org/authors/andrew-free/, here: https://atlpresscollective.com/author/free/, and here: https://assets.aclu.org/live/uploads/2024/06/2024-07-01-ICE-Detainee-Deaths.pdf. 
2. As ICE has rapidly increased its detained noncitizen population since January 2025, mortality in ICE custody has also rapidly increased. 
3. ICE is presently on track to allow more people to die in the agency's custody than in any year since FY2020, when the COVID19 pandemic ripped through facilities claiming lives until federal judges ordered targeted depopulation over ICE's objections. 

Table 1: Publicly Reported Deaths in ICE Custody by Fiscal Year since PBNDS 2011 adoption.
FY	COUNT of FY
11	10
12	8
13	9
14	6
15	7
16	10
17	12
18	10
19	9
20	22
21	5
22	3
23	4
24	12
25	10

4. Public reports indicate Congress intends to appropriate a roughly 900% increase in ICE detention funding, spending $45 billion to expand the deadly detention system. https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/07/us/politics/trump-administration-immigrant-detention-facilities-services.html. 
5. Timely access to information regarding healthcare outcomes in ICE custody is essential to public health researchers, medical experts, policymakers, and informed citizens who wish to have a meaningful role in the policy debate over whether the proposed budget increase represents a lawful and prudent expenditure of public resources. 
6. My previous FOIA work on ICE detention morbidity and mortality has resulted in obtaining records that have been shared with and cited by physicians, oversight agencies, Congress, and courts, influencing decisions that led to healthier outcomes for ICE's detained populations, and reducing the morbidity and mortality in ICE custody. 
7. There is an urgent need to inform the public regarding IHSC's capacity to manage and oversee medical emergencies and conditions that could lead to deaths of people in ICE custody. 

I respectfully request a fee waiver, as I will be publishing and circulating the results of the records I receive, and am not making this request for commercial purposes. 

Thank you in advance for your timely consideration of this time-sensitive request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICFO-36738 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your 5/12/2025, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for records pertaining to IHSC's capacity to manage and oversee medical emergencies and conditions that could lead to deaths of people in ICE custody.  Your request was received in this office on 5/12/2025. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA 
regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your 
request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, 
ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. 
Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA 
regulations, as they apply to media requesters.  As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free.  We will construe the 
submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of 
releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed 
with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a 
right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies 
as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives 
and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2025-ICFO-36738. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office

Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: AER - MA Department of Public Health
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

All adverse medical event records filed with the Massachusetts Department of Public Health between Jan. 1, 2023 and Jan. 1, 2025.

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michael Nolan

Michael Nolan.

title: City of Bixby Opioid Settlement Funds

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: City of Bixby Opioid Settlement Funds
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in the City of Bixby. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

communications.subject: South Carolina Public Records Law Request: Public Records Request: Hanshaw Emails
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Metadata for email communications where Chief Michael Hanshaw is either the sender, recipient, CC'ed, or BCC'ed, sent between the dates of 01/01/2026 and 08/18/2026 and containing at least one of the following keywords: "LPR", "ALPR", "license plate reader", "plate reader", and "Flock Safety".

The specific metadata data points I'm interested in are: to address(es), from address, cc address(es), bcc address(es), sent date/time, received date/time, subject line, and names of all attachments. This request does not seek the contents of the emails themselves, and only the specified email metadata. Please do not include duplicate emails. Please provide me with the records in an Excel format.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Sincerely,

M

(CA. Gov’t Code §7920.000 et seq.)


Re: PUBLIC RECORDS ACT REQUEST RECEIVED ON ­Monday, August 10, 2026

The City of Santa Cruz responds to your public records request for information received on ­Monday, August 10, 2026, as indicated below.

Under the California Public Records Act (CPRA) you are entitled to copies of identifiable, non-exempt public records (Govt. Code section 7922.530). Please note that the CPRA requires the City to provide access to, or copies of, records responsive to your request which are in its possession, subject to certain exceptions. ☒ Government Code § 7922.535(c)(3) • The need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another agency having substantial interest in the determination of the request or among two or more components of the agency having substantial subject matter interest therein.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Marin County Bit Focus Contract and HMIS Contract Information
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The current and any prior contracts or service agreements between Marin County and Bitfocus, Inc. for Clarity Human Services / HMIS, or any contractor used to manage Marin County's HMIS including any amendments, statements of work, and pricing schedules.
2. Any technical documentation, specification sheets, or vendor materials describing the Clarity Human Services API(s), including but not limited to API access policies, authentication/authorization requirements, scope limitations, and data fields accessible via API.
3. Any records, policies, or correspondence regarding whether and how Marin County has configured or evaluated Clarity's "customer portal" feature (or any other client-facing access feature) for individuals enrolled in HMIS.
4. The County's current HMIS Privacy Plan, Policies and Procedures, and any Client Data Inspection, Access, or Correction policy describing how an individual client can request to view, inspect, or correct their own record in HMIS.
5. Any data-sharing agreements between Marin County and third-party agencies or systems (e.g., Medi-Cal managed care plans, county behavioral health, CalAIM/Whole Person Care initiatives) that involve data originating from or shared with HMIS/Clarity.
6. Any records discussing client-facing mobile or web applications, pilots, or proposals related to HMIS, whether internal to the County or proposed by Bitfocus or other vendors.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Ventura County Public Records Coordinator:
Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Government Code § 7920.000 et seq., I request copies of public records concerning Ventura County and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office (“VCSO”) acquisition, installation, operation, administration, use, oversight, and sharing of information obtained through Flock Safety automated license plate recognition (“ALPR”) cameras and related Flock Safety technology.

For purposes of this request, “Flock/ALPR information” includes information collected through Flock Safety cameras, ALPR systems, Flock Safety software and databases, and any related vehicle-location, license-plate, vehicle-characteristic, alert, or investigative information.

This request includes Flock/ALPR systems operated, owned, leased, funded, administered, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO, including systems located in unincorporated areas of the County, County Service Areas, and other areas where the County or VCSO has responsibility for or access to the system.
It also includes records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's access to Flock systems or Flock/ALPR information maintained by another governmental agency, private entity, municipality, school, business, neighborhood organization, or other third party.
1. Contracts, agreements, and financial records
All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, invoices, amendments, renewals, extensions, proposals, quotes, statements of work, and other agreements between Ventura County, VCSO, or any County department and Flock Group, Inc., Flock Safety, or any related Flock entity.
All records concerning the County's initial acquisition or implementation of Flock Safety ALPR technology, including Board of Supervisors agenda materials, staff reports, recommendations, presentations, resolutions, approvals, and related documentation.
All records concerning the acquisition or implementation of Flock cameras through County Service Areas, Municipal Advisory Councils, grant-funded programs, Sheriff's Office programs, or other County-administered programs.
All records reflecting the total cost of the Flock program, including installation, equipment, software, licensing, subscriptions, maintenance, replacement, upgrades, cellular/data service, storage, and other associated costs.
All invoices and payment records relating to Flock Safety from the beginning of the County's relationship with Flock through the date this request is processed.
All records concerning grants, state or federal funding, donations, private funding, County Service Area funds, or other sources used to acquire or operate Flock cameras.
All records concerning any proposal, quote, bid, solicitation, procurement, or competitive process relating to the acquisition of Flock technology.
2. Number, location, and operation of cameras
Records identifying the total number of Flock Safety ALPR cameras currently operated, owned, leased, funded, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying the location of each Flock camera, including installation addresses, intersections, street locations, geographic coordinates, or other location information sufficient to identify where each camera is installed.
Records identifying the date each camera was installed, activated, deactivated, relocated, replaced, or removed.
Records identifying the type and model of each Flock camera or device currently or previously deployed by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying which cameras are located within incorporated municipalities but are accessible by, operated by, funded by, or otherwise connected to Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning any proposed expansion, reduction, relocation, replacement, or modification of the County's Flock camera network.
3. Policies, procedures, and legal authority
The County's and VCSO's current and all prior Flock Safety/ALPR usage and privacy policies.
All policies, directives, general orders, standard operating procedures, training materials, manuals, instructions, or other documents governing the access, search, use, retention, sharing, dissemination, or deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the County official, Sheriff, employee, unit, or other person responsible for custody, administration, oversight, or implementation of the County's Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the job classifications, positions, units, employees, contractors, or other persons authorized to access Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning training required or provided to personnel who have access to Flock/ALPR information, including privacy, civil liberties, data security, ALPR operation, appropriate-use, and data-sharing training.
All legal opinions, memoranda, analyses, correspondence, or other records concerning the legality or constitutionality of the County's or VCSO's use of Flock Safety ALPR technology.
All records concerning compliance with California Civil Code §§ 1798.90.5–1798.90.55 and any other applicable California or federal law governing ALPR technology or surveillance systems.
4. Board of Supervisors, public approval, and public notice
All Ventura County Board of Supervisors agenda packets, staff reports, presentations, minutes, recordings, resolutions, ordinances, notices, and other records concerning the County's decision to implement, continue, expand, renew, or modify its Flock ALPR program.
All records concerning public meetings of the Board of Supervisors, Municipal Advisory Councils, County Service Areas, or other County bodies at which Flock Safety or ALPR technology was discussed.
All records concerning opportunities provided to the public to comment on implementation or operation of the County's ALPR program.
All records identifying the date and meeting at which the governing body provided or considered public comment concerning implementation of the ALPR system.
All correspondence received from members of the public concerning Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
5. ALPR searches and access
Records sufficient to show the number of searches or queries conducted through the County's Flock system, broken down by month, from the beginning of the program through the date this request is processed.
Records sufficient to show the number of Flock/ALPR searches conducted by each authorized user, employee, unit, department, or agency, to the extent such information is maintained.
Records of access to ALPR information maintained pursuant to California Civil Code § 1798.90.52, including the date and time of access, query terms or data elements used, username or identifying information of the person conducting the search, affiliated organization, and stated purpose for the search.
Records concerning audits, reviews, investigations, or monitoring of employee or contractor access to Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any unauthorized, improper, excessive, or suspected misuse of the Flock/ALPR system or its data.
All records concerning complaints, disciplinary actions, investigations, or corrective actions involving improper access or use of Flock/ALPR information.
6. Data retention and deletion
Records establishing the County's current retention period for Flock/ALPR information.
All policies, procedures, technical settings, contractual provisions, or other records governing the retention and deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
Records sufficient to establish whether Flock/ALPR data is automatically deleted after a specified period and, if so, the applicable retention period.
Records concerning any exceptions to the County's standard retention period, including circumstances in which data is retained because it is associated with an investigation, criminal case, evidence, warrant, subpoena, litigation hold, or other legal purpose.
Records sufficient to show the volume or amount of ALPR data retained by the County, if such records are maintained.
7. Data sharing and outside access
All records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's participation in any Flock Safety national, regional, statewide, or multi-agency data-sharing network.
All agreements, memoranda, policies, authorizations, correspondence, or other records concerning sharing of Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data with other law enforcement agencies or public agencies.
Records identifying every outside agency, department, task force, or governmental entity that has been granted access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data or with which Ventura County or VCSO has shared such information.
Records concerning any access by outside agencies to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data, including records sufficient to identify the agency, date, purpose, and type of access, to the extent maintained.
Records concerning any requests by outside agencies for Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any sharing, transfer, disclosure, or access to Flock/ALPR information by federal law-enforcement agencies or federal governmental entities, including but not limited to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), or any federal task force.
All records concerning whether Ventura County or VCSO has enabled, disabled, accepted, rejected, or otherwise participated in any Flock Safety national database or nationwide data-sharing functionality.
All records concerning any requests for or access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information relating to immigration enforcement, immigration investigations, reproductive healthcare, political activity, protests, demonstrations, or other constitutionally protected activity.
8. Flock Community Network and privately owned cameras
All records concerning the County's or VCSO's use of or participation in Flock Safety's Community Network Access or any substantially similar Flock feature.
Records identifying privately owned Flock cameras, including cameras operated by businesses, homeowners' associations, schools, neighborhood organizations, or other private entities, to which County or VCSO personnel have direct or indirect access.
All agreements, authorizations, policies, correspondence, or other records concerning the County's or VCSO's ability to request or obtain access to privately owned Flock camera feeds or Flock-generated information.
Records sufficient to identify the number of requests made by County or VCSO personnel for access to privately owned Flock cameras or feeds.
Records sufficient to identify the number of privately owned Flock cameras or camera feeds available to County or VCSO personnel through the Flock platform.
Records concerning whether privately owned Flock cameras are included in any County or VCSO searchable database, map, network, or investigative platform.
9. Flock Safety system capabilities and configuration
All records describing the capabilities and functions enabled on the County's Flock system, including the types of vehicle information, license plate information, vehicle characteristics, location information, images, alerts, or other data collected.
Records identifying which Flock Safety products, modules, software features, databases, or services are enabled for Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning use or availability of Flock's vehicle search, vehicle fingerprinting, hot-list, alert, sharing, analytics, or other investigative functions.
Records concerning any integration between Flock Safety and other County or law-enforcement systems, databases, records-management systems, computer-aided dispatch systems, camera systems, or investigative platforms.
Records concerning any use of Flock data in connection with facial recognition, biometric identification, person identification, predictive policing, artificial intelligence, or other automated analytical technology.
Records concerning Flock's Vehicle Fingerprint or similar vehicle-identification technology as configured or used by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning automated alerts generated through Flock, including alerts associated with NCIC, NCMEC, hot lists, stolen vehicles, wanted persons, missing persons, or other databases.
10. Effectiveness and results
All reports, statistics, analyses, presentations, or evaluations concerning the effectiveness of the County's Flock program.
Records sufficient to identify crimes, arrests, citations, stolen-vehicle recoveries, missing-person recoveries, investigations, prosecutions, or other law-enforcement outcomes that the County or VCSO attributes to information obtained through Flock/ALPR technology.
Any cost-benefit analyses, performance evaluations, return-on-investment analyses, or assessments of whether Flock cameras have achieved the County's stated objectives.
Any reports or records concerning false alerts, inaccurate plate reads, misidentification, system errors, or other reliability issues involving Flock technology.
Records concerning instances in which Flock information was used to initiate, support, or materially advance an investigation, arrest, search warrant, surveillance activity, or other law-enforcement action.
11. Security and data breaches
All records concerning cybersecurity incidents, vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, data breaches, system compromises, or other security incidents involving the County's Flock system or Flock/ALPR data.
All notices, reports, correspondence, investigations, or assessments concerning any actual or suspected unauthorized disclosure or access to Flock/ALPR information.
Records concerning security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or other security assessments of the Flock system, to the extent such records are not exempt from disclosure.
12. Communications concerning Flock
All emails, memoranda, letters, text messages maintained as public records, meeting notes, and other correspondence between County/VCSO officials or employees and Flock Safety representatives concerning the County's Flock program.
All communications between County/VCSO officials or employees and other governmental agencies concerning Flock Safety, ALPR technology, data sharing, privacy, retention, surveillance, or related issues.
All communications concerning concerns, complaints, objections, privacy issues, civil-liberties issues, or legal issues relating to Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
All communications between Flock Safety and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office concerning access to, sharing of, or searches of Flock data maintained by other law-enforcement agencies.
13. Grant-funded cameras and County Service Areas
All records concerning the acquisition, funding, installation, operation, and maintenance of Flock cameras using state, federal, County Service Area, or other grant funding.
All grant applications, grant awards, grant agreements, reimbursement requests, grant reports, and grant-related correspondence concerning Flock Safety cameras.
All records concerning the three Flock license plate readers reported as approved and installed in Oak Park, including records concerning their funding, installation, ownership, operation, maintenance, data retention, and access.
All records concerning any Flock cameras proposed, approved, funded, or installed in Oak Park, Oak View, or any other unincorporated Ventura County community.
All records identifying the governmental entity or department that owns the cameras and the governmental entity or department responsible for the data generated by those cameras.
14. Current status
Records sufficient to establish whether Ventura County and/or VCSO currently intends to continue operating the Flock Safety ALPR program.
All records concerning any proposed renewal, amendment, expansion, termination, suspension, or replacement of the County's Flock Safety contract or program.
Any current Flock Safety contract, renewal agreement, amendment, or other document establishing the County's present contractual relationship with Flock.
Records concerning any change to the County's Flock program, privacy policy, data-sharing practices, retention period, or access permissions since January 1, 2026.
Request for electronic production
Please provide responsive records electronically in their native electronic format where reasonably available, including searchable PDF, Excel/CSV, or other native formats for databases, spreadsheets, logs, and reports.
For records that exist in a database or other electronic system, I request an electronic export of the responsive data rather than screenshots or summaries, where reasonably practicable.
For access logs, audit logs, query logs, event logs, hot-list reports, and similar electronic records, please provide the underlying electronic records in a machine-readable format where reasonably available.
I am requesting existing records and am not asking the County to create a new record or answer questions. Where a requested record is maintained in a database or other electronic system that can reasonably be queried or exported, please provide the resulting electronic record to the extent permitted by the California Public Records Act.
Segregation of exempt information
If the County believes any responsive record contains information exempt from disclosure, please provide all reasonably segregable portions of the record after redacting only the information specifically exempt from disclosure, pursuant to Government Code § 7922.525.
If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon for each withheld record or portion thereof and provide the factual basis for the claimed exemption. Please also identify the name and title/position of each person responsible for the denial, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.
If the County contends that records are exempt under the California Constitution, Government Code, Evidence Code, Penal Code, Civil Code, or any other statute, please identify the specific statutory provision relied upon.
If records are withheld pursuant to the catch-all exemption or another balancing test, please provide the County's specific justification demonstrating why the public interest served by withholding the records clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure.
Search and response
Please construe this request broadly to include records maintained by:
• Ventura County Sheriff's Office
• Ventura County Executive Office
• Ventura County Board of Supervisors
• County Counsel
• County Information Technology Services
• County Procurement/General Services
• County Auditor-Controller/Treasurer-Tax Collector, where applicable
• County Service Areas
• Sheriff's Office command staff
• Sheriff's Office investigations/divisions
• Any other County department, division, unit, employee, contractor, or agent reasonably likely to possess responsive records
Please also include responsive records maintained on behalf of the County by Flock Safety or another contractor to the extent those records constitute public records subject to disclosure.
If responsive records are maintained by VCSO rather than the County's central records system, please treat this request as applying to both entities and route the request accordingly rather than requiring a new request.
If the County believes this request is overly broad or requires clarification, please contact me promptly and identify the specific portion that requires clarification rather than denying the request in its entirety.
I request that the County comply with the California Public Records Act's applicable response deadlines, including Government Code § 7922.535.
If responsive records are available on an existing County website, please provide the direct location of those records; however, I request electronic copies of records that are not readily accessible online.
Please preserve all potentially responsive records while this request is pending.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Juiciest

title: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Special Event Overtime Data (Boston Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Special Event Overtime Data (Boston Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

8/27/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records. 

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing the all Time and Labor Reports and Overtime Reports for special events and non-detail non-court overtime records for all Boston Police Department employees from January 2020 through present. Please provide all fields used in the tracking system for these cards, including:
City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number
Rank
District/Taskforce
Assigned description
Charged description
Overtime date
Overtime code and description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours
Amount paid

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. 

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”). 

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (781) 915-8324 and mmcsharr@bu.edu.

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a). 

Sincerely,
Mikaela McSharry
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mikaela McSharry

Re: Public Records Request of 08/31/2026 ., B-2026-1474 
  
 Dear Mikaela McSharry 
  
 The Boston Police Department (Department) has received your request for public records. This response applies only to records that exist and are in the custody of the City. See A Guide to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, p. 32, n.115. It is expected that a custodian of records must use her superior knowledge of her records with respect to responses to public records requests. 950 CMR 32.04(5). Specifically, you requested: 
  
 To Whom It May Concern: Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records: 8/27/2026 Dear Records Custodian: This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records. I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing the all Time and Labor Reports and Overtime Reports for special events and non-detail non-court overtime records for all Boston Police Department employees from January 2020 through present. Please provide all fields used in the tracking system for these cards, including: City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID) Employee first name Employee last name Employee middle name Badge Number Rank District/Taskforce Assigned description Charged description Overtime date Overtime code and description Start time End time Worked hours Billed hours Amount paid I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations. If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”). If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv). If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (781) 915-8324 and mmcsharr@bu.edu. Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a). Sincerely, Mikaela McSharry BU SPARK! I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage. I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires. Sincerely, Mikaela McSharry Upload documents directly: https://url4102.request.justfoia.com/ls/click?upn=u001.nrfdmL-2B1UhWpB4V2ArB2sX-2FUeO8LEWs7vXOgof-2Bk4pAI8eXK5X-2B2lXXQMFCyAfRlu2vMbWDG1Ml8DtZf80RV0A-3D-3DJmba_AgUlnmXDYUsn7sCrKgKN3QH-2Bhq41nvd1xNdsQ5Ngv-2FByeojmEVwNGlJMDz-2FIfSSQ3ngiGJBa8UgoylJ1rn5bng4ng28g5DAJtAjKYn5-2F-2BpfoTvLjj-2FIHEwBQ4sI7-2FPxUqY2s-2FU5eeDj4CgJvBKPGaCyAT9fw8461yrRufN9FU8e6DFzw-2Fokir21r-2BhFNQ7KBYUJAg4tV4P75ZtZVpA24hC-2F7oa51Z2gvVl4wtA5h88l2viCPtqQnT3C-2FXtNZiSWJJeTrmtQDUGMr-2B4CQvVEalRVMC4skFeMjvLHy9dnKcja-2Ba6QoymVsRQAeg2HpENzaYci13C4CG7fW2pz5dGHHYw-3D-3D 
  
 We have reviewed our files and have located records that correspond to your request. These records have been shared with you. 
  
 You may appeal this response to the Supervisor of Records in the Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth. G. L. c. 66, § 10A (c); G. L. c. 66, § 10(b)(ix); 950 CMR 32.08; 950 CMR 32.08(1)(h) (in petitioning the Supervisor, the requester shall provide a copy of such petition to the records access officer associated with such petition). You may also appeal to the Superior Court. 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c).

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: LIHTC Detroit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Properties located within the City of Detroit that have received, been allocated, reserved or otherwise been associated with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, including federal 9% credits and 4% credits.

For each LIHTC project located in Detroit, please provide the following information, if maintained:

- Project name and any prior or alternate project names
- Complete street address and ZIP code
- Project identification number, application number or allocation number
- Current owner name
- General partner, managing member, developer, sponsor or affiliated entity names
- Number of total residential units
- Number of LIHTC-restricted units
- Credit type, including 9% credits, 4% credits or other applicable category
- Date of allocation, reservation, award, placed-in-service date or other relevant program date
- Credit allocation amount or annual credit amount, if available
- Current compliance or extended-use status, if maintained
- Any recorded expiration, termination, foreclosure, transfer, ownership-change or other status information concerning the project’s LIHTC restrictions

If MSHDA maintains a master list, project inventory, allocation list, compliance database, or similar report containing this information, please provide that record rather than requiring the information to be compiled manually.

The requested time period is from the beginning of the LIHTC program through the date this request is processed. If a full historical search is not reasonably available, please provide the complete records currently maintained by MSHDA and identify the earliest date covered by those records.

This request seeks existing public records and does not require MSHDA to create a new record or answer questions. If the requested information is maintained in multiple records, please provide the records in the form in which they are ordinarily maintained.

If MSHDA determines that the request is too broad or needs clarification, please identify the specific concern and provide an opportunity to narrow or clarify the request before denying it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: PRR log MSP
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I request a copy of the Department's existing electronic log or list of the public records requests it has received, including for each entry the date the request was received, a brief summary or description of the request, the name of the requestor, and the status or resolution of the request, for the period January 1, 2024 through the date this request is fulfilled.

I am not seeking law enforcement records, criminal offender record information, or any underlying case files. I seek only the administrative log describing the public records requests your office has received — information of the kind that is frequently available from other public sources.

If the log is maintained electronically, please provide it in its existing machine-readable format (for example, CSV or Excel). Producing the existing electronic export should require no segregation or redaction time.
For your reference, the following may bear on the handling of this request:

- In SPR 17/1115 (December 4, 2017), after in camera review, the Supervisor found that a log describing the public records requests received by the Department is not exempt under the CORI Act or G.L. c. 41, § 97D, and ordered the Department to produce the records unredacted.
- This category of record has already been produced by the Department in unredacted form (SPR 17/1115), which defeats any categorical exemption claim.
- To the extent any privacy exemption under G.L. c. 4, § 7, cl. 26(c) is considered, that interest is overcome where the same information is available from other public sources. See PETA v. Dep't of Agric. Res., 477 Mass. 280, 292 (2017).

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian McCarter

communications.subject: RE: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request #P005953-060126
communications.communication:
Dear Supervisor of Records:

I appeal the Massachusetts State Police's response to my public records request of June 1, 2026, reference P005953-060126, which asked for the Department's existing electronic log of the public records requests it has received since January 1, 2024, in the machine readable format in which it is already kept. A response was due June 15, 2026. The Department's only response came on August 31, 2026, the same morning I wrote to ask about the delay, and its entire substance is this: "Please be advised the Public Records Unit processes requests in the order they are received. Due to the high volume of requests we receive daily, we have not yet had a chance to process your request. We appreciate your patience as we diligently work through this high-volume queue." That is a response, but not the one the law requires. It produces nothing, identifies no records, asserts no exemption, describes no search, assesses no fee, and names no date by which the Department will act. G.L. c. 66, section 10(b) and 950 CMR 32.06(2) require each of those things, and they set the deadline without regard to how many other requests the Department has in its queue. The volume of an agency's own backlog is not a ground recognized anywhere in the statute or the regulations for deferring a response, and a custodian that needs more time must say so within the ten business days and give a good faith date, not answer eleven weeks late with an open ended request for patience. A response that supplies none of the required content is a constructive denial. The record sought is a single existing export of an administrative log, that the law requires them to have, the same category of record the Supervisor ordered this Department to produce unredacted after in camera review in SPR 17/1115 (December 4, 2017). I ask that you find the August 31 letter deficient and order the Department to produce the log within ten business days in its existing machine readable format.
