communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: BPD Roster and Officer Photos
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

In CSV/excel format, roster information for all officers who have been employed by Boston Police Department since June 2025.

Some important fields may include:
- City of Boston Employee ID (6-digit ID)
- Badge Number
- Officer First, Middle, Last Name
- Officer Rank
- Sex, race, age if available
- Officer Photo

If any portion of this request is exempt, I request all segregable non-exempt data fields be released.

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. 

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”). 

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (781) 915-8324 or adasuss@bu.edu.

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 business days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident location, area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

Dear J. Ader:

Thank you for submitting your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to
the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) via the
*FOIAOnline* website.
We received your request on September 28, 2020.  Your request concerns an
FBI file.

Our office uses the *FOIAonline* portal for FOIA and Privacy Act requests
for the National Archives and Records Administration's *operational* records
(records created by this agency).  Your *FOIAOnline *request is for records
that may be *archival* records (records created by or originated in a
different agency but that may have been transferred to the legal custody of
NARA), to which access is restricted. Therefore, we have forwarded it to
our *Office of Research Services, Special Access and FOIA* (RF) staff who
handle FOIA requests for such archival records.

Since *Research Services* does not process FOIA requests through
*FOIAOnline*, we removed your request from the *FOIAOnline* website.  *Special

to you. In the future, if you need to follow up with that office directly,
please contact them at the address below, or electronically via email.

The National Archives and Records Administration
Special Access and FOIA Staff (RF)
8601 Adelphi Road, Room 5500
College Park, MD 20740

By email: specialaccess_foia@nara.gov

public, and you can access our online catalog.

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and pursuant to guidance received from the

normal operations to balance the need of completing its mission-critical

safety of our staff.  As a result of this re-prioritization of activities,

request. We apologize for this inconvenience and appreciate your
understanding and patience.

Sincerely,
Susan Gillett

communications.subject: Re: [21-26886] Freedom of Information Act Request - J Ader
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader,

This is in reply to your Freedom of Information Act request, dated
September 29, 2020 for records relating to Frank Teruggi, Jr., including
FBI case file 100-HQ-474363. Your request was received in this office on
April 8, 2020 and assigned the case number 21-26886.

Your request for FBI records has been referred to our Special Access and
FOIA office. They will provide a separate response.

The National Archives at College Park may also hold a Department of Justice
case file for Teruggi. We hold litigation case files of the *Department of
Justice in Record Group 60: General Records of the Department of Justice*.
These records are arranged into numerical classes based on the infraction
of the law involved, and we have various name indexes that allow us to
locate cases pertaining to specific individuals.

Unfortunately, we cannot conduct a search for these records right now. Due
to the COVID-19 pandemic and pursuant to guidance received from the Office
of Management and Budget (OMB), NARA has adjusted its normal operations to
balance the need of completing its mission-critical work while also
adhering to the recommended social distancing for the safety of our staff.
As a result of this re-prioritization of activities, we are unable to
provide a substantive response to requests that require us to consult the
records at this time. We apologize for this inconvenience and appreciate
your understanding and patience.

We also located responsive records in the Department of State Central File,
1973-1979, which is part of *Record Group 59: General Records of the
Department of State*. The Central File is the primary source for
documentation on U.S. foreign policy and events in various countries.
Documents created between 1974 and 1979 exist in an online database that
contains the telegrams and other correspondence of the Department of State.
Many of these documents are open and available online. You can view the
results of our search, access the documents, and conduct your own searches
here
<https://aad.archives.gov/aad/free-text-search-results.jsp?cat=WR43&bc=sl&q=teruggi&btnSearch=Search&as_alq=&as_anq=&as_epq=&as_woq=>
.

The telegrams are full-text searchable. The P-Reels, which contain
documents other than telegrams, are available in paper at the National
Archives at College Park. The P-Reel indexes are also available online. If
you see P-Reel Index numbers that are of interest to you in the set of
responsive records we linked to above, please let us know so that we may
help you obtain those documents. Documents numbered P80 and later must be
requested through the Department of State.

A helpful guide to the 1973-1979 Central File is located here:
https://www.archives.gov/research/foreign-policy/state-dept/rg-59-central-files/1973-1979.html

We also identified an additional series of responsive State Department
records:

Record Group 59
Records Relating to Horman and Teruggi Litigation, 1961 - 1977
<https://catalog.archives.gov/id/27499859>
Entry UD-14D 86

This series is classified and records in the series need to be reviewed for
categories of information exempted from disclosure under the Freedom of
Information Act (FOIA). We are transferring your request to the National
Declassification Center staff for further action. The National
Declassification Center staff will be in contact about the status of your
request.

If you are searching for records relating to Teruggi's murder by the
Chilean military in the aftermath of the 1973 Chilean coup, many records
related to the coup were declassified and released as part of the Chile
Declassification Project. A searchable database
<https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=CHILE&searchText=*> of
these records is available on the State Department's website, and a search
of the database for "Teruggi" yields over 600 hits. The records in the this
database may overlap with some of our holdings, but it is likely that it
also includes material that either has not yet been transferred to us or
that is not available online through the National Archives.

If you have any questions about this database, please contact the
Department of State.

We will continue to process your request when the National Archive resumes
normal operations. For updates on our status, please visit
https://www.archives.gov/coronavirus.

Sincerely,

David Castillo
Archives Specialist
Textual Reference Archives II Branch (RR2RR)
National Archives at College Park, MD

I am writing in response to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request
of September 29, 2020 for records in the custody of the National Archives
and Records Administration. Your request was received in this office on
September 29,2020 and assigned FOIA tracking number RD 64700, interim
tracking number RF-319.

You requested access to FBI file number 100-HQ-474363 on Frank Teruggi, Jr.
Our initial assessment is that Frank Teruggi is the subject of the records,
created between October 1972 and December 1972, and consisting of 9 pages.

We were able to review this file in triage because it was under 10 pages.
We completed a line-by-line review of the records you requested and
released information to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of
our review:

The statute in support of this (b)(3) withholding is 50 USC 3024(1), which

A copy of 100-HQ-474363 is attached.

You also requested FBI case files related to Frank Teruggi, Jr. We
conducted a search of all available FBI indexes transferred to the National
Archives for Frank Teruggi, Jr. and were able to identify 1 additional FBI
case file that is responsive to your request: 100-CG-53422. Our initial
assessment is that Frank Teruggi is the subject of the record, created
between October 1972 and FEbruary 1975, and consisting of an estimated 100
pages.

These records require review for information protected from release under
the FOIA (https://www.archives.gov/foia/foia-guide#determine).

Your request does not exceed 700 pages, so it is assigned to our first-tier
processing queue. Taking into consideration our existing backlog, we
estimate it will take 39 months to complete processing. Once we notify you
that processing is complete, you may either visit our College Park, MD
facility to view the file at no cost, or order a reproduction. Our current
fee for reproductions is 80 cents per page, so we estimate the total cost
will be $80.

You must notify this office of changes to your contact information. If
communication is returned as undeliverable and no return address is
provided, your case will be administratively closed. To change your contact
information or to track the status of your request, please email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. Please include your FOIA
tracking number in all communications concerning this request.

communications.subject: NARA FOIA RD 64700
communications.communication:
Dear J Ader,

I completed processing the records you requested from the National Archives
and Records Administration under Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) tracking
number RD 64700.

You requested access to FBI file numbers 100-HQ-474363 and 100-CG-53422 on
Frank Teruggi.

On May 14, 2021, our office provided a complimentary copy of FBI file
number 100-HQ-474363.


I completed a line-by-line review of the records you requested. Please be
advised, I have considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing
records and applying FOIA exemptions for this request. Information was
released to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of my review:

Records Requested Total Pages Pages Released in Full Pages Released in Part
100-CG-53422 39 28 11

I withheld information protected under section (b) of the FOIA (5 U.S.C.
552). The specific reasons for the denials are:


TYPE OF INFORMATION WITHHELD

FOIA EXEMPTION or STATUTE

classified national security information

(b)(1)

information exempted from disclosure by statute

the statute in support of this (b)(3) withholding is

50 USC 3024 (i)(1), which protects sensitive intelligence sources and
methods

(b)(3)

identities of confidential sources

(b)(7)(D)

You or your designated representative may view the file at the National
Archives at College Park, Maryland. We require at least one week advance
notice to prepare for your visit and ask that you email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov with your FOIA tracking number (RD 64700) and
the date you plan to visit. Please monitor our web page
https://www.archives.gov/college-park for details and updates, as the
operating status for the facility could change, affecting opening hours for
the research rooms.


If you cannot visit our College Park facility, you may order a digital or
paper reproduction copy of the file at the cost of 80 cents per page. To
place a reproduction order, please forward this response to our office
email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. A
mailing/billing address is required to generate a price quote, so please
include that information with your reproduction request.


It is possible the fees to hire a researcher may be less than the
reproduction fees. If you are unable to visit and you wish to hire a
researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher
can be found at this link: https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help. The
National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list.


If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by
regular U.S. mail or by email. By filing an appeal, you preserve your
rights under the Freedom of Information Act and present the deciding agency
with an opportunity to review your request and reconsider its decision. If
you submit your appeal by regular mail, it should be addressed to the
Deputy Archivist of the United States (ND), National Archives and Records
Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road, Room 4200, College Park, Maryland
20740-6001. Both the letter and envelope should be clearly marked “FOIA
Appeal.” If you submit your appeal by email, please send it to foia@nara.gov,
addressed to the Deputy Archivist, with the words “FOIA Appeal” in the
subject line. If you exercise your right to appeal, please explain why you
believe this response does not meet the requirements of the Freedom of
Information Act. All communications concerning this request should
reference your FOIA tracking number.

If you would like the opportunity to discuss my response and attempt to
resolve your dispute without initiating the appeals process, you may
contact our FOIA Public Liaison for assistance:

communications.subject: Virginia Freedom of Information Act Request: Contract Request: Interfolio (University of Virginia)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Virginia Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Elsevier relating to the licensing of Interfolio;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, and/or data processing agreements; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Elsevier for faculty information system technology;
and
Assessment documentation such as the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) related to Interfolio. 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Interfolio.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tom Nash, a citizen of Virginia, in coordination with Michele Gibney.

To the FOIA Officers and Executive Leadership of D.C. DOEE and DDOT:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally demanding the immediate release of all site-specific compliance documents mandated under the District's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Master Permit (No. DC0000221) regarding two active Ward 8 hazard sites: 1488-1600 Morris Rd SE and the stagnant pond located at Hunter Place SE.

Timeframe of Requested Records: January 1, 2022, to the date of final search execution.

This request encompasses the following mandatory disclosures:

1. Outfall Inspections & Maintenance Logs:
All maintenance logs, illicit discharge screenings, structural inspections, and repair work orders conducted by DOEE or DC Water for the stormwater outfalls and conveyance systems directly feeding the Hunter Place SE pond and the severed infrastructure at 1490-1600 Morris Rd SE.

2. Stormwater Retention Non-Compliance:
All internal DOEE, DDOT, and DC Water communications regarding MS4 compliance failures, uncontrolled runoff, or topographic collapse at these specific coordinates.

3. Capital Improvement Project (CIP) Exclusions:
Any internal records, memorandums, or funding directives explaining why the failing infrastructure at these two sites was systematically excluded from D.C.'s mandated MS4 annual reporting and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) remediation plans.

4. FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees. Disclosure of this information is in the primary public interest to inform District residents, federal environmental regulators, and investigative media at WUSA9 regarding systemic MS4 permit violations in Ward 8. The requester is a community advocate with zero commercial interest in these materials.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA Request – Acquisitions, Appraisals, and Third-Party Coordination (CRGNSA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Description of Records Requested:

I request copies of the following agency records from the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area (CRGNSA) office and Region 6 Lands & Realty staff, generated between January 1, 2020, and the present date:

1. Appraisal Instructions & Review for "Birkenfeld/Alashik" (Parcel 03090000760000)
- The Request for Appraisal Services (Statement of Work) and Appraisal Instructions sent to the third-party appraiser for the property identified internally as "Birkenfeld" or "Alashik."
- All correspondence regarding the inclusion of a "Hypothetical Condition" or "Extraordinary Assumption" treating the property as General Management Area (GMA) land while it was legally zoned Special Management Area (SMA).
- The Technical Appraisal Review Report (TARR) and any internal "Review Appraiser" notes approving or questioning this zoning assumption.
- Specific Search Target: Emails between Nicole Carver, Holly Chapman, Jen Barnett, or Donna Mickley and Friends of the Columbia Gorge (FOCG) staff (Dan Bell, Kevin Gorman) in December 2024 and February–March 2024.

2. Grant Application "Drafting" & Coordination (LWCF)
- All draft versions of Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) project narratives or proposal forms for the "Mountain Glade," "Cape Horn," or "Birkenfeld" acquisitions, specifically showing "track changes," comments, or edits originating from external email domains ending in @gorgefriends.org.
- All communications regarding the "Threat to Integrity" or "Urgency" scoring criteria for properties already owned by Friends of the Columbia Gorge.
- Specific Search Target: An email dated roughly August 30, 2022, from Dan Bell to Miki Fujikawa/Holly Chapman regarding the removal of the word "required" and insertion of "wiggle room" regarding trail relocations.

3. "Partner-Funded" Appraisals & Financial Agreements
- All Collection Agreements, Reimbursable Agreements, or correspondence authorizing Friends of the Columbia Gorge to pay for, reimburse, or directly contract the federal appraisal for the "Windy Bluff," "Rowena Bluff," or "Birkenfeld" properties.
- All records discussing the use of "escrow fees" or "closing costs" to reimburse FOCG for property taxes incurred during their ownership period (specifically regarding the Rowena Bluff closing in January 2020).

4. Demolition & Environmental Compliance (Catherine Creek/Windy Bluff)
- All internal engineering notes, emails, or "categorical exclusion" documentation regarding the decision to waive physical site visits or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESA) for the demolition of structures at Catherine Creek (File C24-0002) or Windy Bluff.

Specific Search Target: Emails from Frances Fischer to Jen Barnett in March 2025 regarding "handling this without a site visit."

Search Terms to Apply:
"Birkenfeld", "Alashik", "03090000760000", "Mountain Glade", "Windy Bluff", "Rowena", "Hypothetical Condition", "GMA", "SMA", "Wiggle Room", "Squishiness", "Partner Funded", "Dan Bell", "Renee Tkach".

Fee Category:
I request a waiver of all fees. The disclosure of this information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government—specifically, how federal Land and Water Conservation Funds (LWCF) are valued and prioritized in the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jarrod McClean

communications.subject: Response
communications.communication:
Dear Requestor, 
  
 The City of Azusa is in receipt of your California Public Records Act (“CPRA”) request related to Flock Safety data received on June 11, 2026: 
  
 Under the CPRA, the City’s obligations are to (1) identify the existence of responsive records, (2) determine whether the record or records are disclosable, and (3) if applicable, identify the legal basis for any exemption from disclosure. (See California Government Code, § 7922.540, subds. (a)-(c). The CPRA provides for the inspection or copying of existing identifiable public records; it does not require the City to create records. (See Government Code § 7920.530(a); City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal. 5th 608. 616–627, 629; Haynie v. Superior Court (2001) 26 Cal. 4th 1061, 1075). If information is withheld or redacted, the City need only identify the legal grounds for nondisclosure (Id.) 
  
 The City has (1) identified the existence of responsive records, and (2) has determined that some of these records are disclosable. These records will be produced on a rolling basis. Records, however, which relate to precise location of the City’s ALPR readers are exempt from disclosure under Government Code § 7923.600, subd. (a) because they constitute records revealing law-enforcement security procedures and operational deployment strategies. Disclosure of precise ALPR locations would compromise the effectiveness of the City’s ALPR program by enabling individuals to identify surveillance coverage, avoid detection, exploit coverage gaps, or otherwise undermine law-enforcement operations. The CPRA does not require disclosure of records that would reveal such security procedures or operational vulnerabilities of a local police agency. 
  
 To the extent any portion of the request seeks generalized information about the City’s use of ALPR technology, the City will produce non-exempt, high-level information that does not disclose precise locations or deployment details. Further, some of these records are also exempt from disclosure under the public-interest balancing test set forth in Government Code section 7922.000. Disclosure of precise ALPR camera locations would create a substantial risk to public safety and to the integrity of ongoing and future law-enforcement operations by exposing sensitive surveillance infrastructure and coverage limitations. That risk clearly outweighs any incremental public interest served by disclosure of exact deployment locations. 
  
 The police investigation files exemption encompasses video, audio, and/or other electronic media. Body worn camera video, like any other audio, video or other electronic media taken during a law enforcement inquiry is considered evidentiary material. Like any other piece of evidence connected to a law enforcement investigation, it is not subject to disclosure under the CPRA. Williams v. Superior Court (1993) 5 Cal.4th 337, 361-362. 
  
 Finally, to the extent responsive documents contain Attorney Client Privilege and or Attorney Work Product information they will be redacted or withheld pursuant to Government Code section 7927.705. 
  
 Preparing these documents for disclosure requires the City to review and redact exempt, private, and/or privileged material. These documents are being prepared for public release on a rolling basis. The City will endeavor to provide you with the first set of responsive documents on or about July 13, 2026. 
  
 Thank you, 
  
 Patricia Tachias 
  
 Police Services Administrator

title: FOIA Request — Five South Six LLC Payment of Village Legal Fees

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: FOIA Request — Five South Six LLC Payment of Village Legal Fees
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq., I request copies of records concerning whether Five South Six LLC has been asked, required, agreed, or otherwise discussed paying or reimbursing the Village of La Grange's legal fees and expenses associated with the lawsuit brought by Jonathan Robinson concerning the development at 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue.

Please provide records from January 1, 2025 through the date of your search responsive to the following:

Communications between the Village and Five South Six LLC, or their respective representatives, concerning payment, reimbursement, indemnification, or defense of the Village's legal fees or expenses relating to the Robinson lawsuit.
Any requests, demands, notices, tenders of defense, agreements, or other records in which the Village asked or required Five South Six LLC to defend, pay, or reimburse the Village for legal fees or litigation expenses.
Any records showing whether Five South Six LLC has agreed, refused, disputed, or otherwise responded to any request that it pay or reimburse the Village's legal expenses.
Invoices, payment records, reimbursement records, or other financial records sufficient to show whether Five South Six LLC has paid or reimbursed any portion of the Village's legal fees or expenses associated with this lawsuit.
Any non-privileged records reflecting a Village determination or discussion concerning whether Sections 11.C or 11.D of the Development Agreement require or permit Five South Six LLC to pay the Village's legal expenses associated with this lawsuit.

For clarity, the contractual provisions prompting this request are Sections 11.C and 11.D of the Development Agreement for 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue. Section 11.C provides that the Developer agrees to "hold harmless, indemnify, and, at the election of the Village, defend" the Village against claims connected with the Village's review and approval of the development, issuance of approvals, and development or construction. Section 11.D further provides that the Developer agrees to pay the Village's expenses, "including legal fees and administrative expenses," incurred by the Village in defending against such claims, subject to the provision's limitation concerning the Developer's own acts or omissions.

I am not requesting privileged attorney-client communications or attorney work product. I am requesting the underlying non-privileged records showing whether the Village has invoked, discussed, negotiated, or sought to enforce these contractual provisions with Five South Six LLC.

If responsive records contain exempt material, please provide the reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. 5 ILCS 140/7 provides for disclosure of non-exempt portions of records containing exempt information.

Please provide the records electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Concerned Citizen of La Grange

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1.	A description of all “hot lists” or “custom hot lists” currently maintained for use in Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) systems.
2.	Any policies, agreements, or data-sharing documents identifying external data sources used to populate those lists (e.g., DMV data on suspended/revoked licenses, NCIC, CLETS, Amber Alerts, stolen vehicle databases).
3.	The criteria under which plates are added or removed from hot lists.

Please provide documents in native electronic form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse
